facts.fact: Bianca 的约会对象是个呆子，于是她来电约她探公司；即使只是陪她、或觉得她需要个项目分心，有 Bianca 和 Julie 陪着让她「把他们赶出城」的愿望更像公义、不那么私人。
facts.anchor: Bianca’s date turned out to be a square, so she called me to make plans to visit Manhattan Remediation. Even if she was humoring me, or if she thought I just needed a project to keep from going crazy

facts.fact: Bianca 近来有不好的预感：像有什么事要变糟；她回：那只是湿气。
facts.anchor: I got a bad feeling these days,” Bianca said, sounding distant. “Like something’s about to change for the worse.”

facts.fact: 她扮不成职业装：自己的衬衫都破旧缺扣，Mark 的衬衫胸围不合；最终穿海军条纹水手衫加店里顺来的夹式耳环，对镜自语「至少这是个明确的女人」。
facts.anchor: In the end, I wore a navy striped sailor shirt and a pair of clip-on earrings I nabbed from work. I looked in the mirror and said, Okay, at the very least, this is clearly a woman.

facts.fact: Bianca 给她戴上假发帽：「要官僚风真我得有假发」——她立刻发痒。
facts.anchor: Yes, if she wants Bureaucracy Realness,” Bianca said, fitting a wig cap to my head. I immediately felt itchy.

facts.fact: Julie 冒充「Interboro Housing Authority」，称收到多户住宅遭无证人员进入的投诉。
facts.anchor: We’re with the Interboro Housing Authority,” Julie said, tapping her short nails on our prop clipboard. “We’ve received complaints about unlicensed personnel entering multi-unit buildings.”

facts.fact: 秘书 Marta 反驳：不是热线，就我一个人；不记得接过 NYCHA 的电话。
facts.anchor: It’s not a hotline, it’s just me. And I don’t recall getting any calls from NYCHA.”

facts.fact: Rick 毫不动容，甩出合同卷宗：与城中最大地主（三一教堂、纽约总教区）签约，还在争取 Union Square BID 合作。
facts.anchor: Rick, however, was entirely unbothered, which pissed me off. He dropped a stack of files on the desk. “Afternoon, ladies. I hear you wanted to see our paperwork. These are our contracts with the city’s top landowners, including Trinity Church and the Archdiocese of New York. We’re also securing a partnership with the Union Square BID.”

facts.fact: 她的判断修正：没有秘密政府阴谋，只是生意；但据她所知，下城最大地主是市政府（大量楼被法拍）。
facts.anchor: So there wasn’t a secret government conspiracy, like Bianca had thought—it was just business, although maybe there was less of a difference these days. Still, as far as I knew, the top landowner downtown was the city, since so many buildings were foreclosed.

facts.fact: Rick 说：我们是私人承包商，新租户与业主会主动打电话来，但大部分生意「由楼方做」。
facts.anchor: But most of our business is done by the building.”

facts.fact: 她拼出传单来源：Rick 找上她从没见过的房东——影子层层传回「楼里死了人」；一个月后又是一单，就在隔壁。
facts.anchor: I pictured Rick approaching my landlord, whom I’d never met. A shadow passing from Rick to the landlord to the super, the super telling the landlord telling Rick that there was a death in the building. Then a month later: We got another one, boss, right next door to the last.

facts.fact: Julie 抛法条（纽约州刑诉法 1.20 条第 34 款第 2 项）：既然你自称私人承包商，我们有权关停不合规经营——她微笑。
facts.anchor: under New York State Criminal Procedure Law, section 1.20, subsection 34, paragraph 2, we have the authority to shut down noncompliant commercial operations, since, as you say, you’re a private contractor.”

facts.fact: 看到公司运作如此平庸令她彻底沮丧：只是生意——换句话说，对他们而言毫无意义。
facts.anchor: There was something about seeing Manhattan Remediation run as such a mundane operation that made me feel totally dejected. It was just business, which is another way of saying it meant nothing to them.

facts.fact: 即便两位最老的朋友在身边，那件事又击中她胃部：她最好的朋友走了；若他在，只会叫她别再这样。
facts.anchor: Even with my two oldest friends by my side, it hit me again, right in the stomach, that my best one was gone. If he were here he would just tell me to stop.

facts.fact: Bianca 说：有权势的人迷信；鬼不过是他们砸钱摆平的又一种麻烦。
facts.anchor: Powerful people are superstitious. Ghosts are like any other problem they throw money at to make go away.”

facts.fact: Julie：当权力站在骗子一边就很难；我同情你。
facts.anchor: It’s hard when power is on the side of the con men. I sympathize.”

facts.fact: Julie 的主意：回仓库关掉他们的系统，让他们亏到关张——但没有具体办法。
facts.anchor: Maybe we go back to the warehouse, shut down their system, and set them back so bad they’re in the red and gotta close up shop.”

facts.fact: Star 从未回电；Bianca 惊道：Cris 说她去了你家。
facts.anchor: “What do you mean? Cris said she left for your apartment.”

facts.fact: Bianca 眼睛睁大又似退到脑后；过马路被出租逼回人行道，手按心口闭眼镇静后说：出事了。
facts.anchor: Then she said, her eyes still shut, “Something happened.”

facts.fact: Johnny 的公寓无人应答，邻居说男友两天前匆忙搬走；门未锁，屋里空无一物、异常干净、留着漂白水味；没有 Star 的痕迹。
facts.anchor: It was oddly clean, a whiff of bleach left behind. No trace of Star.

facts.fact: 他们在空屋站了一分钟：他走得匆忙却还有空打扫——她不信他在担心押金。Bianca 说：我得去你家打几个电话。
facts.anchor: We stood in the emptiness for a minute. He had left in a hurry but made time to clean. I didn’t think it was his security deposit he was worried about.
